chunks: So Moses returned to his people full of anger and regret. He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord make you a good promise? Did the covenant seem too long to you, or did you wish for the wrath of your Lord to fall upon you, so you broke your promise to me?'
ai.seo_question: What did Moses say to his people when he returned from Mount Sinai?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Taa-Ha, Prophet Moses (AS) returns to his people with a dual emotional state of *ghadab* (anger) and *asafan* (regret), reflecting the Shia scholarly view of his human-like yet infallible leadership during the calf incident. He challenges the Israelites by reminding them of God's initial promise and questioning whether their breach of covenant with him was a deliberate choice to incur divine wrath, thereby highlighting the link between prophetic authority and communal obedience.
